admission.justification: Both restarting from the install and ignoring the mismatch were weighed and rejected, and every later install now has to keep the preflight, the late-restart answer and the irreversible-site guard in agreement.

alternatives.option: The install step reads whether a stop would be needed before any write and defers with restartRequired and the terminal remedy; explicit `paseo provision` remains the transition that may restart.
alternatives.reason: An install must be safe for a user who is working; the session loss is then a deliberate, named, out-of-host action instead of an install side effect.

alternatives.option: Let the install step restart a mismatched host, as the old direct provision did.
alternatives.reason: Any install run by an agent of the host would kill the session that called it, and sessions of other agents would be closed without warning.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A host restart preserves running sessions and turns, or every install is guaranteed to run outside the host.

alternatives.option: Install the new version while the old host keeps running and note the mismatch only in the log.
alternatives.reason: The install would report success while the running host is not the build's host, and a later start would find an inconsistent install.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host and its clients are proven to tolerate a mixed install.

consequences: A build that moves the host release needs a terminal provision before the host matches the build; the install says so and changes nothing of the host.
A live provider or setting change that the daemon applies without a stop is still applied.
context: runtime_install is called by the tool server, which is a child of the host's worker, so a provision started from it stops its own process halfway; a restart closes every agent session, running turns and pending permission prompts.
decider: architect's refinement under D75, frozen in MIK-R96@v1 rule 9
